name: Tm Visualization Suite: Process Explorer
pitch: Follow every order through its steps, and see where it waits, loops or takes a detour.
question: How do cases move through a process, and where do they get stuck?
useWhen: Show how cases move through steps over time.
features: See each case as a row of events
Line up the steps of many cases

hero.alt: Swimlane chart of order events grouped by team: customer, payment, store, customer service and carrier.
hero.caption: Who holds the order at each moment, team by team

screenshots.alt: State transition diagram of order steps with arrows between them, thicker where more cases pass.
screenshots.caption: A state diagram shows which step follows which, and how often

screenshots.alt: Trace chart of the carrier's orders, one row per order with its delivery steps and the total time at right.
screenshots.caption: Select a team and the trace shows only its orders

questions: Where do orders wait the longest?
Which paths do cases take, and how often?
Where does the process loop back or fail?
audience: Analysts and BI leads who study how orders, tickets or cases flow through a process.

featureStrips.heading: See each case as a row of events
featureStrips.text: A trace gives every order its own row, with each step on the time axis, so slow cases are easy to find.
featureStrips.alt: Trace chart with one row per order and its steps as dots and bars on a time axis.

featureStrips.heading: Line up the steps of many cases
featureStrips.text: An event sequence orders the steps of each case, so you compare how different cases unfold.
featureStrips.alt: Event sequence of order steps listed in order with a dot at the time of each step.

featureStrips.heading: Mark the moments that matter
featureStrips.text: Milestones show when each case reaches a key stage, so you see which cases reach it late.
featureStrips.alt: Milestone chart with one row per order and a mark where it reaches each stage.

featureStrips.heading: Follow the typical journey
featureStrips.text: A journey chart lines the cases up by stage, so you see which stage each one reaches and when.
featureStrips.alt: Journey chart with orders as rows and stages Order, Payment, Fulfilment, Delivery and After-sales as columns.
